sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Arrays are your first step into organizing data like a pro! Let's explore how they work and why they're essential.

• What arrays are and why we need them
• How to create and use arrays in code
• Simple real-world examples to make it click

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine a toolbox with labeled slots - that's an array! Each slot holds one item, and you can access any item instantly by its number.

Arrays are like:
• A row of mailboxes (each with a number)
• A parking lot (each spot has a number)
• A classroom (each seat is numbered)

In programming, arrays let you store multiple values of the same type together. Instead of creating 10 separate variables for 10 numbers, you create one array that holds all 10 numbers!

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how arrays work:

steps.title: Creating an Array
steps.description: We declare an array that can hold 5 integers. Think of it as reserving 5 parking spots.

steps.title: Storing Values
steps.description: We put values into each 'slot' (called an index). Remember: counting starts at 0!

steps.title: Accessing Values
steps.description: We can get any value by its index. Here we get the value at index 1 (which is 20).
steps.code: int value = numbers[1]; // value is now 20

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Arrays store multiple values of the same type
✓ Each value has an index (starting at 0)
✓ Arrays have fixed size once created
✓ Use square brackets [] to access elements
✓ Great for organizing related data together

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use arrays for similar data (like test scores)
Initialize arrays with values when possible
donts: Don't forget arrays start at 0, not 1
Don't try to store different data types
Don't access indices outside the array size
Don't create arrays bigger than needed
sections.protip: Use array.length to get the size - it's your safety net against out-of-bounds errors!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where are arrays used in real apps?

examples.how: Store lists of products, prices, or customer orders in arrays
Keep track of scores, inventory items, or player positions
Manage lists of posts, friends, or notifications
Store temperature readings for different days

problem.description: Create an array to store 5 of your favorite movies. Then write code to print the third movie in the list.
hints: The third movie is at index 2
Use quotes around each movie title
problem.explanation: We created an array with 5 movie titles. The third movie (Avatar) is at index 2 because we start counting at 0. Easy peasy!

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Arrays store multiple values in one variable
📌 Always remember: first element is at index 0
📌 Ready to learn about loops with arrays next!
